approved: Hazardous Waste (Regulation of Exports and Imports) Amendment Bill 2016
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a two-bill package that would overhaul how Australia regulates hazardous waste shipments.
The package would let the government charge fees covering the full cost of running the permit system for importing, exporting and transiting hazardous waste.
A separate levy bill would recover shared administrative costs that cannot be linked to a single permit applicant.
The bill would amend the Hazardous Waste (Regulation of Exports and Imports) Act 1989 to allow full cost recovery of the permit scheme.
The bill would streamline administrative processes, such as publishing permit applications and decisions on the department's website instead of the Commonwealth Gazette.
The bill would reduce regulatory costs for business.
Businesses that apply for permits to import, export or transit hazardous waste, and the waste generators who ultimately pay the fees.

The Hazardous Waste (Regulation of Exports and Imports) Amendment Bill 2016 and Levy Bill 2016 implement Australia's Basel Convention obligations, allow full cost recovery for permitting, and lift the $8,000 cap on waste imports/exports to ensure cost recovery, while the speaker also urged reducing the $500 billion national debt and returning the budget to surplus.

The bill introduces administrative efficiency reforms and cost recovery measures for hazardous waste permit schemes, shifting costs from taxpayers to waste movers by raising permit fees and imposing an indexed levy.
